newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end weaker on cash, fund pressure.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end weaker on cash, fund pressure.

text.p: Fund selling and renewed concern over seasonal weakness in cash cattle prices knocked CME live cattle futures to mostly lower closes, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.825 cent per lb lower to 0.025 higher with only distant December up and nearby December pacing the loss at 68.075 cents. Feeders ended 0.125 to 0.350 cent lower with January off the least at 67.275 cents a lb.
Fund profit taking and new selling added to renewed concern over topping action in cash markets to push values into sell stops, traders said.
Although choice fed cattle supplies remain tight, packers may ease bids in view of other market factors, traders said.

"Packers have a little more (live) inventory into this week and can hold out longer," said Jim Clarkson, analyst for A and A Inc. "There are more numbers ahead and Thanksgiving is a weak period for cash cattle."

Choice boxed beef values showed some weakness Friday after posting the highest prices last week since August, 1993. The slip Friday may indicate the beef market is nearing a high. However, choice beef cuts again showed strength and was quoted at $118.67 per cwt, the highest level since August 17, 1993.

Refco, R.J. O'Brien, ADM Investor Services and RBH notably sold early while Prudential Securities and Merrill Lynch sold late after buying early, traders said. Dean Witter at Refco also sold late, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, traders sold December 68 to 70 calls on the break in futures and sold December 68 puts at the futures low. December volatility was steady at 14.5 percent. Commercials added April by buying 64 puts and selling 68 calls, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle were influenced by both live cattle and corn futures and ended with small losses in light trade.
Spillover pressure from live cattle erased early gains in feeders after values in that pit were boosted by lower corn futures and a higher CME feeder cattle index, traders said.
The latest index rose $0.14 to $64.98 per cwt, the highest since December 26, 1995.

R.J. O'Brien and Smith Barney bought January feeder cattle early and locals sold later, traders said. Cargill Investor Services spread long August feeders/short December live cattle, pit sources said.
